The guard is suspended before forwarding AcquireSRWLockExclusive, before setting its input guard to -1 and before constructing GMalloc.

exe_import.name: _initterm
exe_import.semantics: EXE CALL reaches a JMP through its _initterm IAT. The thunk is not an additional live callback frame. API-set descriptor identity is not proof of the resolved implementation module.

callback_loop.meaning: Loads RAX from the current table slot, skips null, calls the dispatch thunk, advances the cursor only after the callback returns. At the suspended callback return PC, RBX still identifies the active slot and RDI the original end.

dispatch_tail_chain.tail_semantics: CALL 0xf8010 -> JMP 0xed6a0 -> JMP [guard-dispatch cell] -> on-disk default JMP RAX -> callback. No dispatch stub pushes a return address; only _initterm+0x36 remains below the callback. The first thunk has no .pdata; the latter two have zero-operation unwind records, not additional live callback frames.
dispatch_tail_chain.os_cfg_override: Windows may replace the guard-dispatch pointer. The disk default is not a live-value assertion. The minimally supported strict implementation may require the relocated default pointer and matching JMP RAX bytes. A different current target requires separate authenticated tail-dispatch semantics, otherwise reject; do not accept arbitrary ntdll/System32 frames. No such override target was inspected live or qualified here.

minimum_authentication_algorithm: Keep all existing exact UAL handoff, primary-thread, EXE frame/register, code and cold-state predicates. This section replaces only the former external CRT gap.

Parse the authenticated EXE import descriptor/name and exact thunk; read its current _initterm IAT value without invoking it. Resolve the actual mapped-image owner from trusted current module/mapping information, not basename or a guessed address. Require the corresponding authenticated System32 ucrtbase file and its named non-forwarded _initterm export. Current IAT must equal that export VA; IAT/GetProcAddress equality alone does not finish authentication.

Authenticate the actual module's file identity and PE/export/exception metadata against its backing disk file. This artifact qualifies only the supplied CRT fixture. A different CRT file requires equivalent reviewed callback/unwind semantics, not reuse of these fixture RVAs by OS-version guess.

Compare the relevant loaded function, dispatch-tail and unwind bytes with their on-disk counterparts after applying legitimate relocation handling where needed. Derive the primary runtime-function identity from the named export and PE exception directory; require the recorded no-CHAININFO unwind semantics in this fixture. Reject hooks, mismatching code, forwarders or incomplete exception metadata; never skip a frame to recover the expected sequence.

For the minimal default-dispatch case, require the current load-config guard-dispatch cell to point to this module's relocated disk-default JMP RAX target and verify the tail bytes. Reject an unqualified runtime override. This check is not a request to invoke CFG or any callback.

Native-unwind the FName constructor using the already required EXE records. The immediately following frame must be the authenticated _initterm primary function at the exact decoded callback return (fixture RVA 0x707d6), not any PC in that function or any frame in the same module.

At that reconstructed CRT callback frame require RBX=EXE+0x0556a070 and RDI=EXE+0x055e4a28; copy the current qword at RBX and require EXE+0x00352bb0, with the pinned initializer-table prefix/code unchanged. Preserve the existing FName constructor RBX=EXE+0x06f52300 and NamePool/static-guard register witnesses. These are current reconstructed registers and bounded reads, not historical table membership alone.

Unwind exactly this one CRT callback frame using its authenticated unwind record. The next PC must be EXE+0x0216bfac in the authenticated CRT startup function. Do not expect a frame for the EXE import thunk, the tail-jumped initializer or the CFG dispatch stubs; do not scan past extra frames.
